Its mission is campaigning for the legal rights of nature. Paul specialises in upholding the rights of environmental activists to protest and protect the natural world. raw.full_description: Join us at the Library for the launch of the RIBA Refugee Committee online database. From 1938 the Royal Institute of British Architects (RIBA) received a fastgrowing number of requests for assistance from architects working in Nazioccupied Central Europe. The Papers of the RIBA Refugee Committee, specially set up by the institute in January 1939, include documents and correspondence related to more than 200 individuals (mostly architects) who became known to the RIBA between 1938 and 1941. A result of groundbreaking research on the RIBA Refugee Committee Papers, the database will include entries for each one of these individuals, whatever their fate or their stature. Their lives, their work, their often extraordinary stories will be shared and celebrated through this new international research hub. About the speakers Oliver Urquhart Irvine is Executive Director of Architecture Programmes and Collections at the Royal Institute of British Architects. He leads RIBAs exhibitions and public programmes, awards and honours, library and collections, partnerships and fundraising, and is overseeing the longterm transformation of access to RIBAs collections. Oliver has over 25 years experience working across cultural, heritage and higher education organisations, with a particular focus on libraries, archives, collections, education and digital access. Before joining RIBA, he was Director of the SOAS National Research Library and Director of Learning, Research and Enterprise Services at SOAS University of London, where he was also a Trustee and Principal Investigator on major externally funded research and digitisation programmes. Valeria Carullo is Curator of the Robert Elwall Photographs Collection at the Royal Institute of British Architects. Her principal area of research is the relationship between modern photography and modern architecture in the interwar years. An architect by background, she lectures and writes on both architectural and photographic subjects. In 2019 she published MoholyNagy in Britain 19351937 (Lund Humphries). Valeria has curated and cocurated several exhibitions, including her latest Wide Angle View: architecture as social space in the Manplan series 196970 (RIBA London, 202324, and RIBA Liverpool, 2026). She is the lead researcher of the ongoing RIBA Refugee Committee project and in June 2024 she organised the international conference Displaced Lives: Architects Seeking Refuge on the Brink of WWII. Dr Irena Žantovská Murray HonFRIBA is an architectural historian and curator. In her work, she has focused primarily on exploring aspects of 20th century architecture, with emphasis on the Modern Movement. Professionally, she devoted most of her career to building, advancing and making accessible art and architectural collections, first at McGill University in Montreal and, from 2004 to 2013, as Sir Banister Fletcher Director, British Architectural Library, at the Royal Institute of British Architects. She is currently a Research Fellow at the Faculty of Architecture, Czech Technical University, in Prague. As an editor, coeditor or translator, she has been responsible for publications such as Moshe Safdie: Buildings and Projects (1996), Karel Teige, Modern Architecture in Czechoslovakia (2000), Le Corbusier and Britain (2009) and Guido Beltramini, The Private Palladio (2012). She is the principal external contributor to the RIBA Refugee Committee research project.

raw.full_description: Climate, justice and global challenges: Scotlands role in a changing world. Join us for SIDAs Spring Conference on Tuesday 10th March Were delighted to invite our members and community to join us for our 2026 Spring Conference. SIDAs Spring Conference will bring members together to explore how the accelerating climate emergency is shaping global justice responses and development practice. With a keynote address, panel discussions and interactive workshops, the event will create space for shared learning, practical reflection and networking, focusing on Scotlands role and responsibilities in an increasingly complex global context. Well be returning to the COSLA Conference Centre, right next to Haymarket Station in Edinburgh, and streamed online for those attending remotely. The agenda will include keynote speakers, interactive panel discussions, breakout workshop sessions, and networking opportunities. Arrivals and refreshments from 9:00am with the agenda starting at 9:30am. After the sessions, a networking lunch will be available between 1:30pm 2:15pm. We have lots of exciting opportunities for exhibitors, sponsors and speakers, so if youre interested, please contact Francis Rodgers at the SIDA office for more information. Details are available at https://intdevalliance.scot/events/sidaspringconference2026/

raw.full_description: An elegant blacktie charity gala featuring an entertaining and inspiring lineup alongside a threecourse dining experience for Sudan. Future Voices: The Charity Gala is a blacktie charity evening and a firstofitskind event for our community, bringing together culture, conversation, and collective impact. Presented by The Nile Fest in collaboration with Youth Factor, this event reflects a shared commitment to uplifting the next generation. Future Voices represents the emerging leaders, creatives, and changemakers within our community and the importance of creating spaces where those voices are heard, nurtured, and celebrated. The Nile Fest is a collective dedicated to making culture and creativity accessible while connecting the diaspora to meaningful causes back home. Youth Factor is a longstanding organisation focused on empowering young Sudanese people through events and activities that foster unity and growth. After a period of inactivity, Youth Factor is relaunching with renewed momentum, building on the success of its previous initiatives. This evening aims to bring together youth, professionals, families, and community groups in one inspiring space bridging generations through the arts, dialogue, and shared experiences. The night will feature an entertaining and inspiring lineup, which will be announced gradually through our social media channels. We are proud to be supported by Ethar Relief , whose vital work on the ground in Sudan this gala seeks to support. All proceeds from the evening will go towards furthering their humanitarian efforts. Future Voices: The Gala is a blacktie affair. Guests are encouraged to dress their best and join us for an unforgettable night celebrating community, creativity, and the voices shaping our future.
